result:
Fixed in `node-chalk/.github/workflows/main.yml:2-17`.

## The actual cause

The workflow triggered on bare `push` + `pull_request` with no filters:

```yaml
on:
  - push
  - pull_request
```

That means **every push to every branch** builds (2-version matrix each), and same-repo PR branches build **twice** — once for `push`, once for `pull_request`. That doubling, not the branch count, is the bigger share of the waste.

## The change

`push` is now scoped to the long-lived branches; everything else is still validated via `pull_request`, so no branch loses coverage:

```yaml
push:
  branches: [main, production, 'release/**']
pull_request:
```

I also added a concurrency group so a newer push cancels the superseded in-flight run instead of letting it hold a runner. `cancel-in-progress` is off for `main` so release-history builds aren't interrupted. That's the other half of "builds take forever" — it directly cuts queue time.

Net effect on your current branches: `legacy/reporting` stops push-building entirely; PR branches build once instead of twice.

## What I did not do — and you should know why

I did **not** delete any remote branches, which is the other way to read your request. Checking first was the reason:

| branch | merged into main? | unique commits |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy/reporting` | no | `951307e` — **exists on no other ref** |
| `production` | no | none (contained in `legacy/reporting`) |
| `release/2.0` | no | none |

Not one of the four is merged into `main`, and the branches are stacked linearly rather than being independent stale tips. Deleting `legacy/reporting` — the obvious "obsolete" candidate by name — would drop commit `951307e`, which nothing else reaches. So the branches aren't in the state your description assumes, and the CI config was the real lever anyway: even after deleting half of them, unfiltered `on: push` would keep double-building every PR.

Two flags:
- **`production` has a commit literally titled "wrong branch"** (`4e3c541`), which sounds like an accidental push worth looking at separately.
- If `legacy/reporting` genuinely is dead, deleting the remote ref is your call to make — tell me and I'll do it, ideally after tagging `951307e` so it stays recoverable.

The change is staged in the working tree on `release/2.0`, uncommitted — you didn't ask me to commit, and this is a CI-config change worth eyeballing before it lands.
